title: Agent model picker: OpenRouter model list is not sorted alphabetically
description:
REPRO: Open the Agent settings panel (AgentSettings) → with a valid OpenRouter key configured the Model dropdown loads → the models appear in OpenRouter's raw /models API order, not alphabetical. Hard to scan/find a specific model.

ROOT CAUSE: The parsed model catalog is never sorted; the dropdown renders it in raw API order.
- packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/openrouterClient.ts:116-138 parseOpenRouterModels() iterates payload.data in order and pushes each entry to models[] with NO .sort() — it returns the list exactly in the order OpenRouter's /models endpoint returned it.
- packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/AgentSettings.tsx:183-190 maps load.models directly to <option>s (load.models.map((m) => <option .../>)) with no sort, so the <select> renders in that same unsorted API order.
- Confirmed there is NO alphabetical (or any other) sort anywhere in the agentchat path: the only .sort() calls in packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/ are thread-recency sorts in threadStore.ts (unrelated). No intentional ordering (e.g. recommended-first / current-model-pinned) exists that a sort would disrupt.

EXPECTED: Models listed alphabetically, case-insensitive, by display name (the same string shown in the option, i.e. m.name; fall back to m.id when names collide/are absent).
ACTUAL: Listed in OpenRouter API order (effectively arbitrary for the user).

FIX DIRECTION: Sort the model list case-insensitively by label before rendering. Cleanest spot: sort in the <option> map source in AgentSettings.tsx (e.g. [...load.models].sort((a,b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' }))), or sort the parsed array in parseOpenRouterModels() so all consumers get a stable alphabetical order. Sort by name (case-insensitive); tie-break on id. If product later wants the current/selected model or a 'recommended' model pinned first, pin those then alphabetically sort the remainder — but the core ask is plain alphabetical. Note the '— select a model —' placeholder option must stay first.

PRIORITY: low (UX nit, user-reported). HEAD at filing: 5e1f19c72412ad9a80192b92ba20086b5aa34a49.
